rows.quote_or_number: Keep the documentation up to date. Allow and encourage your readers to give you feedback about what's unclear. Then make revisions based on this.
rows.note: Author advocating for keeping docs current via reader feedback

rows.quote_or_number: you keep the content online, up to date by making sure readers are informed of new developments that might make advice irrelevant
rows.note: Praising author for maintaining online content freshness over time

rows.quote_or_number: I want it to tell me that the point I'm making is technically wrong because an expert would recognize subtle misuse of terminology
rows.note: Writer seeking external feedback on technical accuracy of own writing

rows.quote_or_number: I found reader feedback to be eye-opening. Because I was getting it as I went along, I was able to adapt and change
rows.note: Technical author praising value of continuous reader input during writing

rows.quote_or_number: You'll learn the mechanics... the discipline to finish, and you'll get feedback from readers about what works and what doesn't.
rows.note: Technical author recommending blogging as way to get reader feedback

rows.quote_or_number: When I talk to other bloggers, they're often discouraged that HN ignores everything they submit... they're expressing an interesting idea, but they don't know how to articulate it
rows.note: Blogger noticing peers struggle to get audience feedback on posts

rows.quote_or_number: A technical blog is a teaching tool, and nobody is willing to pay the teachers enough in money, or attention, to make it worth it.
rows.note: Author discussing lack of incentives for maintaining technical blogs

rows.quote_or_number: Good feedback tells you whether the reader learned what you meant to teach. It tells you how hard it was for the reader to learn it
rows.note: Experienced tech writer on necessity of reader feedback for quality

rows.quote_or_number: Do I communicate my ideas clearly and concisely, or are they too confuse and meandering? I typically get useful feedback.
rows.note: Writer actively seeking feedback on writing clarity

rows.quote_or_number: In the old days, we wrote blogs, and got replies days, weeks, months, even years later.
rows.note: Discussing traditional blogging's delayed feedback loop

rows.quote_or_number: it's hard for me to immediately tell whether or not the advice is credible... the inclusion of your full name... would elevate the blog
rows.note: Reader feedback on establishing trust via authorship clarity

rows.quote_or_number: good writing requires... they have access to competent feedback on their own writing.
rows.note: Professional writer noting feedback is essential to good writing

rows.quote_or_number: I can solve the "readers don't want to pay for content any more but content is expensive to produce" problem by getting companies to pay for it
rows.note: Ritza: service providing technical articles for companies seeking quality content

rows.quote_or_number: Once someone buys your book on Leanpub, they get updates to the book for free... you can keep your book up to date when technology changes.
rows.note: LeanPub: platform solving versioning/updates for technical content

rows.quote_or_number: Lean Publishing is the act of self-publishing a book while you are writing it, evolving the book with feedback from your readers
rows.note: LeanPub defining lean publishing model with live reader input

rows.quote_or_number: published a book to help developers write more compelling blog posts... strategies for optimizing all phases of the technical blogging process
rows.note: Writing for Developers book: teaching technical blogging best practices
